# 4 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Seven Brothers Before Antiochus

---

**8:1** The tyrant's argument having been refuted by the noble sentiments of Eleazar's speech, the guards brought seven brothers, handsome and modest and well-born and altogether charming, together with their aged mother.

**8:2** When Antiochus saw them standing in a circle around their mother, he ordered his soldiers to be at the ready while he himself questioned them, saying:

**8:3** Young men, I look favorably upon each of you and I offer my friendship; and I give you my solemn oath that if you will transgress the tradition of your fathers and take up the life of the Greeks, I will make you all princes and will enroll you in the highest positions of my service.

**8:4** And if by your stubbornness you provoke me further, you will force me to destroy each one of you with terrible tortures.

**8:5** Have pity, then, on yourselves! Even I — the very man who is your enemy — have compassion on your youth and your beauty.

**8:6** Will you not reflect and reconsider, turning away from the folly of your ancestral customs?

**8:7** When Antiochus had spoken these words, the eldest son answered for all his brothers, saying:

**8:8** What are you planning to ask of us, and what do you intend to learn from us? For we are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.

**8:9** We would be shaming our fathers if we did not obey the law and take reason as our guide in all things.

**8:10** O king of tyranny! Do not suppose that you can overpower reason in us. We already consider ourselves dead before your tortures begin.

**8:11** We are moved by nothing you threaten us with, for we hold the law to be stronger than all threats.

**8:12** We will not transgress the commandments of our father Moses on any count whatsoever.

**8:13** And you, O tyrant — if you torture us for our disobedience and then put us to death — know that you only make us suffer here for a short time.

**8:14** But you will receive from the divine judgment the eternal torments of fire for your impiety.

**8:15** Are you not ashamed, O man of strength against the powerless, to tear apart the limbs of those who belong to the same nature as yourself?

**8:16** Even if our enemies spare those who are captured and imprisoned, you, our most bitter enemy, make torments of our very flesh.

**8:17** Yet this all confirms for us that reason is sovereign over the passions.

**8:18** For had we been weak and inclined toward passion, we would yield and be led astray by you. But we have been educated in wisdom and strengthened by the law.

**8:19** You must know, O Antiochus, that the laws that were given to our fathers by Moses are our strength, and we will never transgress them.

**8:20** And now, if it pleases you to torture us for refusing, begin!
